message.content: In an abstract world that resembled abstract art, Hedgie the hedgehog with glasses was the only real creature. He stood in a field of swirling color, where trees were made of looping ribbons and the sky shifted from violet to silver like a brushstroke left unfinished. Around him, shapes had no fixed names: a sun that might have been a memory, a river that flowed as a thin line of black ink, and mountains built from stacked fragments of light. Hedgie blinked behind his tiny round spectacles, and the world sharpened just enough for him to feel safe. His small real life depended on the way he looked at impossible colors. When a storm of jagged triangles gathered above him, Hedgie adjusted his glasses and searched for the edge that was still real. The storm was not made of rain or wind; it was made of sudden angles, harsh reds, and sharp opinions that cut across the painted air. Through his lenses, Hedgie saw a single soft blue note caught in the storm’s center, trembling like a living thing. He stepped closer, his spines brushing against the smooth, artless ground, and whispered, “I’m here.” By accepting the strange beauty of his world, Hedgie showed that reality could exist inside abstraction. The storm slowed, the triangles softened, and the lost blue note floated down to rest on one of his spectacles. The abstract landscape did not disappear, but it became gentler, as if it had finally been seen by something real. Hedgie lifted his face, his glasses catching the strange light, and the world around him seemed, at last, less like a painting and more like home.
